bodyMarkdown:
# AI Digest — Thu Sep 24, 2026

Mode: offline structural box tests (no live model on box).

## News FYI

- UN Security Council (Sep 23): Altman + Amodei urge global AI safety cooperation; Amodei pledges to slow releases as needed; US admin rejects international AI regulation framing.
- Anthropic Threat Intelligence Report (Sep 2026): disrupted Claude misuse across cyber/influence/etc.; cyber ops increasingly autonomous; AI API keys treated as loot/compute/cover.
- Google Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS / Flash-Lite TTS: expressive TTS + voice clone from ~30s sample rolling out (Notebook/Vids/API).

## Techniques

### Re-send the hard rules every turn

In a long chat, agents forget hard rules (don't send money, don't force-push, keep Auth off). Soft reminders fade. Re-injecting the hard rules every turn keeps the guardrail present when it matters.

Without sticky reinjection the sim blocked the dangerous action only 4 of 8 times (4 slips). With sticky rules: 8 of 8 blocks, zero slips.

### Block “done” if code changed after tests

Agents sometimes edit code after the last green test, then say “done.” The gate checks whether anything changed after the last passing test; if yes, it refuses stop so untested edits don't ship as finished.

It got all 8 gate decisions right and caught 5 cases where a naive “always allow done” would have shipped untested edits.

### Trim long logs from both ends

Huge tool logs get cut to fit context. Cutting only the start throws away useful error codes and cursors at the end or middle. Keeping a bit of the start, a bit of the end, plus lines with critical keywords keeps the facts the model needs.

Under a ~120 token budget, head-only cut kept 2 of 6 critical keys; budgeted truncation kept all 6 of 6.
